name: MonarchPasswordInput
title: PasswordInput
wrapsNative: SecureField, swapped for TextField while revealed, with .textContentType(.password) or .newPassword
summary: A labelled password field with a toggle that shows the password as text, over the standard SecureField and TextField.
whenToUse: For any password: sign-in, sign-up, reset, or confirming an action.
whenNotToUse: For a one-time code or PIN use MonarchOtpPinInput. For other secrets that must never be shown, use MonarchTextField with isSecure.
api: init(_ label: String, text: Binding<String>, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, purpose: MonarchPasswordInputPurpose = .current, isRevealed: Binding<Bool>? = nil, revealLabel: String? = nil)

options.name: prompt
options.description: Placeholder shown while the field is empty.

options.name: error
options.description: Error message; replaces the helper while present.

options.name: purpose
options.description: current sets the password content type; new sets the new-password content type, so the system offers a strong password.

options.name: isRevealed
options.description: Whether the password is shown as text. Without it the component keeps the state itself, starting hidden.

options.name: revealLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Show password" spoken name of the toggle.

states.name: hidden
states.description: A SecureField, and an eye symbol on the toggle.

states.name: revealed
states.description: A TextField with the password as text, and a crossed eye symbol on the toggle.

states.name: focused
states.description: Draws the theme's focus ring around the field.

states.name: error
states.description: Danger border, and an icon and message under the field.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Subtle background, the disabled text colour and a disabled toggle, set with disabled(_:).

appearance: The same field as MonarchTextField: a surface-coloured field with an input border and 8-point corners, with the reveal symbol in the muted text colour at the trailing edge.
platformNotes: The web warns while Caps Lock is on; iOS has no Caps Lock state to read on the software keyboard, so the hint is dropped. The web has sm, md and lg sizes; iOS has one size, the size of MonarchTextField. The autofill hint is the SwiftUI content type instead of autocomplete.
accessibility: The field is one VoiceOver element: label, then the system's secure value, then the error (spoken as "Error: …") or else the helper text as the hint.
The reveal control is given to VoiceOver as a standard Toggle named "Show password" in both states; its value says whether the password is shown.
A new error message is announced when it appears.
The error is shown with an icon and text, not colour alone.
The field and the toggle each have a 44-point touch target.
edgeCases: An empty error string counts as no error.
Revealing swaps the SecureField for a TextField; focus is moved to the new field when the old one had it.
The system may clear a SecureField when editing starts again after the password was hidden.
Autocorrection and capitalisation are off in both states.

examples.title: Sign in
examples.code: MonarchPasswordInput("Password", text: $password, prompt: "", helper: "The password for your account.", purpose: .current)

examples.title: New password with validation
examples.code:
MonarchPasswordInput(
    "New password",
    text: $password,
    helper: "At least 12 characters.",
    error: password.isEmpty || password.count >= 12 ? nil : "Use at least 12 characters.",
    purpose: .new
)

examples.title: Reveal state held by the screen
examples.setup:
@State private var password = "correct horse"
@State private var isRevealed = true
